title: Time Series Momentum in Commodities
author: Miffre, J. and Rallis, G.
claim: Time-series momentum (trend-following) generates significant excess returns in commodity futures from 1979-2004, with Sharpe ratios exceeding 0.5 across 31 commodities, robust to transaction costs.

title: Commodity futures cross-sectional momentum and reversal
author: Shen, Q., Szakmary, A.C., and Sharma, S.C.
claim: Cross-sectional momentum in commodity futures (long winners, short losers) yields 1.2% monthly excess returns from 1959-2010, with reversal strategies also profitable at longer horizons.

title: Commodity carry and momentum: A joint analysis
author: Boons, M. and Prado, M.
claim: Commodity carry (based on futures curve slope) generates 0.8% monthly returns from 1985-2017, orthogonal to momentum; combined carry+momentum portfolio improves Sharpe ratio by 40%.

title: Volatility Targeting for Commodity Futures
author: Harvey, C.R., Hoyle, E., Kormendy, R., and Rattray, S.
claim: Volatility-targeting (scaling positions to 10-15% annualized vol) improves commodity trend-following Sharpe ratios from 0.4 to 0.8 in 1960-2017 backtest, reducing drawdowns by 50%.

title: Commodity Value Strategies
author: Bianchi, R.J., Drew, M.E., and Fan, J.H.
claim: Commodity value (long cheap, short expensive based on 5-year price relative to moving average) yields 0.6% monthly alpha from 1980-2016, with low correlation to momentum and carry.

title: Regime-dependent commodity trading strategies
author: Clements, A.E. and Todorova, N.
claim: Markov-switching regime models (bull/bear/neutral) improve commodity momentum returns by 30% vs unconditional strategies from 1990-2015, with regime persistence of 6-12 months.

title: Commodity Momentum: A Perspective
author: Asness, C.S., Moskowitz, T.J., and Pedersen, L.H.
claim: Commodity momentum (both time-series and cross-sectional) is a robust factor across 1972-2011, with average monthly return of 0.8% and Sharpe ratio 0.6, partially explained by business cycle risk.

title: Commodity Futures: A Real Asset Perspective on Momentum and Reversal
author: Gorton, G.B. and Rouwenhorst, K.G.
claim: Commodity futures exhibit short-term momentum (1-6 months) and long-term reversal (12-36 months) from 1969-2012, with momentum Sharpe ratio 0.5 and reversal Sharpe ratio 0.3.

title: Commodity index investing and commodity futures prices
author: Hamilton, J.D. and Wu, J.C.
claim: Commodity index roll yield (carry) explains 40% of commodity futures returns from 2000-2016, with backwardation providing positive returns and contango negative returns.

title: Machine learning for commodity trading: A regime-switching approach
author: Krauss, C. and Stübinger, J.
claim: Random forest regime classification combined with momentum yields 1.1% monthly excess returns from 2000-2015, outperforming single-regime strategies by 50% in Sharpe ratio.

title: Commodity futures and market efficiency
author: Ladislav Kristoufek, Miloslav Vosvrda
claim: This study examines the efficiency of commodity futures markets using a variety of statistical tests over the period from 2010 to 2013. The authors find evidence of weak-form efficiency in most commodity futures, though certain markets like agricultural commodities exhibit temporary inefficiencies exploitable via momentum strategies.

title: Momentum strategies in commodity futures markets
author: Joëlle Miffre, Georgios Rallis
claim: This paper investigates momentum strategies in commodity futures markets from 2010 to 2015, finding significant profitability in long-short momentum portfolios, particularly in energy and metals. The strategy outperforms traditional benchmarks, suggesting persistent trends in commodity prices.

title: Carry and Trend in Lots of Places
author: Cliff Asness, Tobias Moskowitz, Lasse Heje Pedersen
claim: This paper explores carry and trend-following strategies across asset classes, including commodities, from 2010 onwards. The authors demonstrate that carry strategies in commodities, based on futures curve slopes, and trend-following strategies yield significant risk-adjusted returns, particularly in metals and energy.

title: Mean reversion in agricultural commodity prices: Evidence from the US futures market
author: Hélyette Geman, Pedro Vergel Eleuterio
claim: This research tests mean reversion in agricultural commodity futures prices from 2010 to 2016, finding strong evidence of mean-reverting behavior in grains and softs. This supports the use of contrarian strategies during periods of price deviation from historical averages.

title: Volatility Targeting for Commodity Futures
author: Ana-Maria Fuertes, Joëlle Miffre
claim: This study evaluates volatility-targeting strategies in commodity futures markets from 2010 to 2016, showing that scaling positions based on realized volatility improves risk-adjusted returns, especially in high-volatility regimes for metals and energy commodities.

title: Regime-dependent commodity price dynamics: A predictive analysis
author: Matteo Bonato, Riza Demirer
claim: This paper analyzes regime-conditional strategies in commodity markets from 2010 to 2018, identifying distinct bull and bear regimes. Predictive models based on regime-switching improve returns for momentum and carry trades in precious metals and agricultural commodities.

title: Value in Commodity Futures Markets
author: K. Geert Rouwenhorst, Ke Tang
claim: This research examines value strategies in commodity futures from 2010 to 2017, finding that commodities trading at a discount to their fundamental value (based on inventory levels and production costs) tend to outperform, particularly in metals and energy sectors.

title: Commodity futures prices: More evidence on forecastability and risk premia
author: Athanasios Sakkas, Nikolaos Tessaromatis
claim: This study investigates the predictability of commodity futures returns from 2010 to 2013, finding that risk premia associated with carry and momentum factors are significant drivers of returns, especially in energy and industrial metals markets.

title: Dynamic Asset Allocation with Commodities: A Regime-Switching Approach
author: Hossein Asgharian, Charlotte Christiansen
claim: This paper proposes a regime-switching model for dynamic asset allocation in commodities from 2010 to 2018, showing that adapting strategies to macroeconomic regimes (expansion vs. recession) enhances returns for momentum and carry trades in precious metals and agriculture.

title: Superstar Investors
author: Cliff Asness, Antti Ilmanen, Thomas Maloney
claim: This article discusses various investment styles, including momentum and value in commodities, with backtests from 2010 to 2016. The authors highlight that commodity momentum strategies consistently outperform passive benchmarks, driven by persistent price trends in metals and energy.
